blocks.text: The articles of opinion ( ⁧مَقَالُ رَأْيٍ⁩ ), editorials ( ⁧اِفْتِتَاحِيَّة⁩ ) and headings ( ⁧عَمُود⁩ ) are the part of the newspaper in which it is discussed: the author supports a thesis, brings arguments, responds to objections and draws a conclusion. For an analyst they are valuable, because they show how to think in a country about a topic; But they must be read knowing how to distinguish the thesis from the arguments, the solid arguments from the weak ones, the apparent concession from the true. In this unit you learn the structure of an argumentative text , the correlations of the cause , consequence , addition and concession ( ⁧فَضْلًا عَنْ⁩ , ⁧وَمِنْ ثَمَّ⁩ , ⁧صَحِيحٌ أَنَّ⁩ … ⁧إِلَّا أَنَّ⁩ …, ⁧وَإِذَا كَانَ⁩ … ⁧فَإِنَّ⁩ ...), the most frequent types of argument and fallacies, and start writing your own argumentative text. Four weeks, in parallel with EGY-15.

2. use and recognize the argumentative connections of fuṣḥā, including concessionary constructions ( ⁧صَحِيحٌ أَنَّ⁩ …
3. classify the arguments (data, e.g. authorities, consequences, comparison) and assess their soundness;
4. recognizing the most common fallacies (generalization, false dilemma, attack on the person);
5. write an argumentative text of 250 words with a clear structure.
